meta.ogDescription: Robotic facade cleaning instead of rope access crews, and robotic floor cleaning: estimated annual savings, payback and 5-year net gain.

head.label: PAYBACK – CALCULATOR
head.title: How much a robot can save.
head.lead: Move the sliders and the numbers update instantly. Based on Moscow market data, 2026.

wage.label: Operator wage
wage.hint: The robot needs a crew of two: an operator and a roof safety attendant certified for work at height. We cost both at this rate.

glass.hint: The robot clears horizontal frames up to 10 mm high. If they are higher, the facade needs an assessment.

staff.label: Current cleaners
staff.hint: Pre-filled from the norm for this area. You can change it.

out.label: Calculation result
out.note: This is an indicative estimate based on Moscow market data and does not guarantee results. We calculate the exact economics after a site assessment.

price.text: per m²: the usual price for rope access cleaning of continuous glazing in Moscow, from public price lists

output.text: per robot per shift. The manufacturer states 1,200–2,000 m² a day

shifts.text: per cleaning season: mid-April to mid-October, excluding rain, wind and weekends

kit.text: turnkey X-Human K3 kit, according to the supplier

steps.compare: We compare it with what you now pay your rope access contractor: glazed area × number of cleanings × price per m².
steps.share: The robot cleans about 90% of the glazing. Rope access technicians finish corners, canopies and obstructed sections at your price.
steps.crew: The robot needs a crew of two: an operator and a roof safety attendant. We cost their wages, including income tax and social contributions, for every shift.
steps.season: The season runs from mid-April to mid-October. A quarter of the days are lost to rain and wind, and work happens on weekdays. One robot handles about 147,000 m² a year. If the volume is larger, we include a second robot in the calculation.
steps.saving: Savings = what you pay the contractor now − robot cost, brushes and consumables, service at 8% of the price per year, and manual touch-up.
steps.fit: The robot works on continuous glazing. We check the facade’s suitability and roof mounting space during the assessment.

steps.payback: Payback is how many months of savings it takes to cover the purchase. The 5-year net gain is the savings over the service life minus the price of the robots.
steps.lease: Leasing: 20% down payment, 36 months. We show how much you keep each month after the lease payment.

wage.text: median cleaner wage in Moscow, from 2026 job postings

payroll.text: social contributions: since 2026, most companies pay 30%

manual.text: of floor one person cleans by hand per shift

robot.text: price of a compact scrubber robot in the Pudu CC1 class

steps.surface: The robot only handles flat hard floors, about 60% of the area in an office. Restrooms, desks and trash stay with people.
steps.freed: We calculate how many full-time positions (FTEs) are freed from floor cleaning, with a margin: 30% of the floor work stays with people.
steps.norm: If you have more cleaners than the norm, each one cleans less, so the same robot frees more FTEs. But never more than half the team.
steps.saving: Savings = wages with contributions + chemicals and water − robot service, consumables and a share of our platform operator’s time.

1.ariaLabel: Sales floor, fall and winter: 5 times a day

2.ariaLabel: Produce, all day: 5 to 10 times a day

frequency.note: As Perekrestok (X5 Group) puts it: this is the chain’s practice, not a sanitary standard.
frequency.service: 10–15 min a day to look after the robot; the docking station does the rest.

0.title: Sales floor and concourse cleaning
0.text: Floor-scrubbing robots wash mall concourses and the sales floor at night before opening, then make repeat passes by day among shoppers.

1.title: Parking cleaning
1.text: Sweeping and scrubbing robots for indoor and underground parking. In the Moscow pilot, robots clean not only the mall interiors but the parking too.

2.title: Promo and wayfinding
2.text: A service robot with an advertising screen carries promos around the floor and shows the way. BellaBot works this way in two Perekrestok stores; according to project participants, sales of some products grow by up to 100%.

3.title: Warehouses, dark stores
3.text: Online order picking and moving goods behind the sales floor is warehouse robotics. It has a page of its own.

case.title: Chains already use floor robots.
case.lead: Named sites and figures come from open sources. These are not our projects but the market track record you can build on.

0.title: Lenta hypermarkets: robots across the country.
0.text: Volgograd, Nizhny Novgorod, Moscow, St Petersburg and other cities. They started with a pilot: 10 robots in 9 hypermarkets, then bought 32 more. Savings come from staff and from dropping rented scrubbers.
0.quote: According to Lenta’s press service, cleaning staff shrank by 30–40%.

1.title: Perekrestok: Pudu CC1 in the chain’s supermarkets.
1.text: 9 stores in Moscow, 1 in St Petersburg, 1 in Sochi (as of June 2024). Caring for the robot with its docking station takes 10–15 minutes a day.
1.quote: 11 tonnes of water a year per store versus 73 tonnes for a manual floor scrubber, according to project participants.

2.title: Central Children’s Store: pilot week one.
2.text: A pilot by FTs BAS under the Moscow Department of Entrepreneurship and Innovation: 26 malls, robots from four Russian manufacturers. They clean interiors and parking lots.
2.quote: The pilot lasts several months, then a comparison with manual cleaning. No results published yet.

meta.title: Professional Robotics products: platform, RaaS, Retrofit
meta.description: Robot fleet management platform, robot rental (RaaS), retrofit of your equipment, AI modules and Open API integration. Professional Robotics products.

hero.title: Professional Robotics products and business models.
hero.lead: Buying a robot is only half the job. Next you have to manage it, service it and know whether it pays back.
hero.text: Our products cover exactly that: a platform to control your fleet, rental instead of buying, retrofit of equipment you already own, and integration with your systems.

platform.title: The platform your whole fleet runs on.
platform.lead: Professional Robotics Platform is our own development. It manages robots of any type and manufacturer, from cleaners to humanoids, and we write the features you are missing for your task.

trust.data: Data in Russia, data center in Skolkovo

board.label: Sample platform dashboard: 142 devices, 14 sites, 98.2% SLA, 24 active operations
board.foot: Cleaning · delivery · warehouse · humanoids on one map

fleet.text: A fleet across several sites from one center: grouping by site and status, bulk commands, remote setup and updates.

dispatch.text: Operations control and task allocation across devices: a map, statuses and errors in real time, failure alerts.

ai.text: Recognition, workflows and operating analytics on top of the base hardware. Our in-house AI agents predict failures before downtime.

api.text: Integration with the client’s ERP, BMS and accounting systems. The platform fits into your infrastructure rather than replacing it.

raas.title: Rental instead of buying. Start without big upfront costs.
raas.lead: Robot rental (RaaS, Robots-as-a-Service) removes the large one-off payment: a lower entry cost, a faster start, pay for use.

entry.title: Lower entry cost
entry.text: A regular payment instead of a big purchase. No need to secure an equipment budget in advance.

start.title: Faster start
start.text: You test the robot at your own site and decide on buying from real numbers.

use.title: Pay for use
use.text: Take one for high season or a pilot and return it when utilization drops. We choose equipment from several brands.

calc.title: Buy or rent: an example
calc.chartLabel: Cumulative cost chart: buying and renting
calc.note: An illustration based on market benchmarks, not a Professional Robotics price list. Buying includes ownership costs (service, consumables, operator time) at 16% of the price per year. We assume rental includes maintenance. We calculate the rate and term for your site.

retrofit.title: Retrofit: equipment you already bought keeps working.
retrofit.lead: We upgrade existing equipment: adding cameras, navigation, sensors and semi-automatic workflows. It’s often faster and cheaper than buying a new robot.

cmp.label: Diagram: what you pay for with a new robot versus a retrofit
cmp.newNote: you pay for the machine and autonomy
cmp.caption: Cost structure, not to scale. At the assessment we work out which is cheaper for your site: upgrade or replacement.

platform.title: Our own platform
platform.text: This is not a vendor license but Professional Robotics’ own Russian development. We connect robots of any brand and write what’s missing. Data stored in Russia, data center in Skolkovo.

ai.text: They predict failures before downtime and reroute cleaning in real time.

service.title: Service across Russia
service.text: Our own service network, working under SLA. The platform spots a failure, service fixes it.

makers.title: Any manufacturer
makers.text: 2–5 vendors per area: we take what fits the task and the economics, not what we hold exclusive rights to.

roi.title: Economics first
roi.text: The conversation starts with your site’s payback.
